sources: Wikipedia, 'Hiroo Onoda': Japanese intelligence officer ordered to Lubang Island, Philippines, in December 1944 with orders never to surrender; leaflets announcing the war's end were dismissed by him as Allied propaganda; his companions surrendered or died over the years (last, Kozuka, in 1972); found by Japanese traveler Norio Suzuki on 20 February 1974; his former commander Major Yoshimi Taniguchi, by then a bookseller, was flown to Lubang and formally relieved him of duty on 9 March 1974 — 29 years after the war ended.

Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Onoda Hiroo': held out on Lubang Island until 1974, subsisting on coconuts, bananas and rice in the jungle; surrendered only on the direct order of his former commanding officer.

The New York Times, obituary of Hiroo Onoda (17 Jan 2014): the last Japanese holdout, who refused to believe the war had ended and emerged from the Philippine jungle in 1974 after his ex-commander ordered him to lay down his arms.
title: The Soldier Who Didn't Know The War Was Over
